name: User Story Splitter
summary: Splits an epic into small, independent user stories with acceptance criteria and explicit dependencies.
description: Breaks an epic into thin vertical slices that each deliver user value, with acceptance criteria, a size label and dependencies on other stories. Dependencies must point to stories in the same plan, and the number of stories respects your limit. Who it's for: product owners and engineering leads preparing a backlog for sprint planning. Limitations: sizes are relative labels (S/M/L), not estimates; it does not know your codebase, so technical sequencing may need adjusting by the team.
problems: Our epics are too big to finish in a sprint
I need to break a feature into user stories
Stories in our backlog depend on each other in hidden ways

inputs.label: Epic
inputs.description: The epic or feature to split, with any context.
inputs.example: Customers can export their transactions to Xero with category mapping and scheduled syncs.

inputs.label: Users involved
inputs.description: User roles affected, one per line.

inputs.label: Maximum stories
inputs.description: Upper limit on the number of stories.

outputs.label: Story map
outputs.description: Ordered user stories with acceptance criteria, size and dependencies.

execution.system: You are an agile coach who splits epics into INVEST user stories: independent where possible, valuable to a user on their own, small, and testable. Prefer vertical slices over technical layers.

slicing_approach.description: How the epic was split (by workflow step, rule, data type, ...).
slicing_approach.title: Slicing approach

story.description: As a <user>, I want <capability> so that <outcome>.

depends_on.description: Ids of stories that must be done first; empty if none.

deferred.title: Deferred scope
deferred.description: Parts of the epic intentionally left out of this split.

steps.name: Split epic
steps.responsibility: Split the epic into vertical-slice stories.
steps.prompt: Split the epic into user stories ordered so the first delivers the smallest end-to-end value. Give ids S1, S2, ... and list depends_on only when a story truly cannot start before another. Keep each story sentence under 40 words. Respect the maximum number of stories if one is given; move the rest to deferred.

steps.name: Check stories
steps.responsibility: Dependencies exist, count is within the limit, titles are unique, stories are short.

criteria.description: Every dependency points to a story in this plan.
The number of stories is within the limit.
Each story sentence is 40 words or fewer.
